review_target: The two local framed-reader source files identified below, compared with the observed local source base. Source files were not edited by this reviewer.

related_checkpoints.provenance: Checkpoint publication verification and prepared tree were reported by the implementation agent; this review independently identifies the source and test blobs below.

source_diff.shape: One private long counter, one public getUncompressedCount override, and one positive-result increment in each framed reader.
source_diff.static_comparison: For each source file, removing exactly those three insertions reproduces the base file byte for byte.

regression_review.method_count_correction: An earlier narrative mistakenly said six shared methods; the actual source has five methods and ten invocations. No test change was required.
fixture_findings: Complete valid first payload followed by one zero byte causes a subsequent framing-read failure: an incomplete four-byte LZ4 signature or a Snappy compressed-chunk tag without its three-byte length.
The between-frame LZ4 skippable frame and Snappy type-0x80 chunk encode two metadata bytes. Neither contributes decompressed output.

The existing mixed.txt.sz fixture contains raw and compressed Snappy chunks, a repeated identifier, padding, and skippable chunks. The IWORK fixture retains its independent expected-output comparison.
Legacy counter equality assertions use a fully consumed single-identifier stream, avoiding repeated-identifier compressed-count assumptions.

correctness_findings: Each getter now reports output returned by successful reads instead of inherited compressed/header-byte accounting; constructor read-ahead leaves the new field zero.

Both increments occur once at the end of the top-level bulk read, only for a positive result and after existing checksum/dependency processing. Single-byte read already delegates to that method and is not counted twice.
Zero-length reads, EOF, and reads that throw before returning add nothing. Output returned before a later framing/checksum failure remains counted.
The field persists across chunks, metadata, and enabled frame concatenation. Public inherited read-based skip counts consumed decompressed bytes; internal raw metadata skips do not touch the field.
All historical count, pushedBackBytes, getBytesRead, getCount, getCompressedCount, decoder, checksum, and framing operations remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
remaining_risks_and_limits: No blocking source issue found. Existing repeated-identifier compressed-count behavior and malformed-stream recovery behavior are outside this change.
